eg: Air pollution in many large cities has become a serious threat to public health.
egCn: 许多大城市的空气污染已成为公共健康的严重威胁。

eg: If more households recycled their glass and paper, far less rubbish would end up in landfill.
egCn: 如果更多家庭回收玻璃和纸张，最终进入垃圾填埋场的垃圾就会少得多。

eg: Climate change is making extreme weather events more frequent in many parts of the world.
egCn: 气候变化正使世界许多地区的极端天气事件更加频繁。

eg: Most scientists agree that human activity is the main cause of global warming.
egCn: 大多数科学家认为，人类活动是全球变暖的主要原因。

eg: Building new roads through forests can seriously disturb local wildlife.
egCn: 在森林中修建新道路可能会严重干扰当地的野生动物。

eg: Large areas of rainforest are cleared every year to make room for farmland.
egCn: 每年都有大片热带雨林被砍伐，用来腾出农田。

eg: Hundreds of plant and animal species are at risk because their homes are disappearing.
egCn: 由于栖息地不断消失，数百种动植物正面临危险。

eg: Rising sea levels mean that coastal towns will face more frequent floods.
egCn: 海平面上升意味着沿海城镇将更频繁地遭遇洪水。

eg: Some cleaning products release chemicals that are harmful to both people and animals.
egCn: 一些清洁用品会释放出对人和动物都有害的化学物质。

eg: Supermarkets throw away tonnes of food waste that could feed people in need.
egCn: 超市扔掉成吨的食物垃圾，而这些食物本可以养活有需要的人。

eg: Cycling to work is one of the most environmentally friendly ways to travel.
egCn: 骑车上班是最环保的出行方式之一。

eg: Many homes in sunny regions now use solar power to cut their electricity bills.
egCn: 如今阳光充足地区的许多家庭使用太阳能来降低电费。

cn: 可持续的；不破坏环境的
eg: Governments should invest in sustainable farming methods that protect the soil for future generations.
egCn: 政府应投资于能为子孙后代保护土壤的可持续耕作方式。

eg: The country aims to produce half of its electricity from renewable sources by 2035.
egCn: 该国的目标是到 2035 年一半电力来自可再生能源。

eg: Stricter rules on factory emissions have greatly improved air quality in the region.
egCn: 更严格的工厂排放规定大大改善了该地区的空气质量。

eg: Burning fossil fuels such as coal and oil releases large amounts of carbon dioxide.
egCn: 燃烧煤和石油等化石燃料会释放大量二氧化碳。

eg: Flying less often is one of the quickest ways to reduce your carbon footprint.
egCn: 少坐飞机是减少个人碳足迹最快的方法之一。

eg: Cattle farming produces a surprising amount of methane, a powerful greenhouse gas.
egCn: 养牛业会产生数量惊人的甲烷，这是一种强效温室气体。

eg: Wildlife conservation projects rely heavily on donations from the public.
egCn: 野生动物保护项目在很大程度上依赖公众捐款。

eg: When forests are cut down, many animals lose their natural habitat.
egCn: 森林被砍伐后，许多动物就失去了它们的自然栖息地。

eg: Tigers are an endangered animal, with only a few thousand left in the wild.
egCn: 老虎是濒危动物，野外仅剩几千只。

eg: Without urgent protection, several kinds of rhino could become extinct within decades.
egCn: 如果不立即加以保护，几种犀牛可能在几十年内灭绝。

eg: A long drought destroyed crops and left thousands of farmers without an income.
egCn: 一场长期干旱毁掉了庄稼，使数千名农民失去了收入。

eg: Visitors who leave litter on the beach should be given heavy fines.
egCn: 在海滩上乱丢垃圾的游客应被处以重罚。

eg: National parks help to preserve beautiful landscapes for future generations to enjoy.
egCn: 国家公园有助于保护美丽的自然景观，留给后代欣赏。

eg: Shoppers are encouraged to bring reusable bags instead of buying plastic ones.
egCn: 商家鼓励顾客自带可重复使用的购物袋，而不是购买塑料袋。

eg: Hotter and drier summers have led to more destructive wildfires in Australia and California.
egCn: 夏季越来越炎热干燥，导致澳大利亚和加州的山火更具破坏性。

eg: During last summer's heatwave, temperatures in the city reached over forty degrees.
egCn: 去年夏天热浪来袭时，城市气温超过了四十度。

eg: Children who live near busy roads breathe in large amounts of exhaust fumes.
egCn: 住在繁忙道路附近的孩子会吸入大量汽车尾气。

eg: Several countries have banned single-use plastic straws and cutlery.
egCn: 一些国家已禁止使用一次性塑料吸管和餐具。

eg: Deforestation not only destroys wildlife habitats but also speeds up global warming.
egCn: 森林砍伐不仅破坏野生动物的栖息地，还会加速全球变暖。

eg: Coral reefs support an extraordinary level of biodiversity in a very small area.
egCn: 珊瑚礁在很小的区域内维系着极其丰富的生物多样性。

eg: Removing a single predator can upset the balance of an entire ecosystem.
egCn: 一种捕食者的消失就可能打破整个生态系统的平衡。

eg: Chemicals from the factory had contaminated the river that supplied the town's drinking water.
egCn: 工厂排出的化学物质污染了为该镇供应饮用水的河流。

eg: Most of the plastic we throw away ends up in landfill, where it takes centuries to break down.
egCn: 我们扔掉的塑料大多被送进垃圾填埋场，要花几百年才能分解。

eg: Old batteries contain toxic metals that can leak into the ground if not disposed of properly.
egCn: 旧电池含有有毒金属，如果处理不当会渗入地下。

eg: Heavy use of pesticides has been linked to a sharp fall in bee populations.
egCn: 大量使用农药被认为与蜜蜂数量锐减有关。

eg: Poaching for ivory remains one of the biggest threats to African elephants.
egCn: 为获取象牙而进行的偷猎仍是非洲象面临的最大威胁之一。

cn: 不可逆转的；无法挽回的
eg: Scientists warn that some damage to the polar ice may already be irreversible.
egCn: 科学家警告，极地冰层受到的部分破坏可能已经无法逆转。

eg: The rapid depletion of groundwater is forcing farmers to drill ever deeper wells.
egCn: 地下水迅速枯竭，迫使农民把井打得越来越深。

eg: Free editing software allows anyone to make professional-looking videos at home.
egCn: 免费的剪辑软件让任何人都能在家制作出专业水准的视频。

eg: Most young people today prefer digital books and music to physical copies.
egCn: 如今大多数年轻人更喜欢数字版的书和音乐，而不是实体版。

eg: The telephone was invented in the nineteenth century and changed communication forever.
egCn: 电话发明于十九世纪，永远改变了人们的通讯方式。

eg: In some factories, robots now do most of the heavy and dangerous work.
egCn: 在一些工厂里，机器人如今承担了大部分繁重和危险的工作。

eg: Many teenagers check their smartphones dozens of times a day without even noticing.
egCn: 许多青少年一天要看几十次手机，自己却浑然不觉。

eg: There is now an app for almost everything, from booking taxis to learning languages.
egCn: 如今几乎做什么都有对应的应用，从叫车到学语言。

eg: Using the same password for every account makes it easy for criminals to steal your information.
egCn: 所有账户都用同一个密码，会让犯罪分子轻易盗取你的信息。

eg: Students can download lecture notes before class and review them on their phones.
egCn: 学生可以在课前下载讲义，然后在手机上复习。

eg: Electronic devices such as tablets have become a normal part of many classrooms.
egCn: 平板电脑等电子设备已成为许多课堂的常见配置。

eg: It only takes a few minutes to install security cameras that you can control from your phone.
egCn: 只需几分钟就能装好可以用手机控制的监控摄像头。

eg: I often browse the internet for news while I am on the train.
egCn: 我坐火车时常常上网浏览新闻。

eg: Online shopping is convenient, but it has forced many small high-street shops to close.
egCn: 网购很方便，却也迫使许多商业街上的小店关门。

eg: Artificial intelligence is already helping doctors to spot diseases earlier than before.
egCn: 人工智能已经在帮助医生比以往更早地发现疾病。

cn: 小器具；小装置；电子小玩意
eg: My father loves buying the latest gadgets, even if he rarely uses them.
egCn: 我父亲喜欢买最新款的电子小玩意儿，即便他很少用。

eg: Most cafes now offer free wireless internet to attract customers.
egCn: 如今大多数咖啡馆都提供免费无线网络来吸引顾客。

cn: 易于使用的；用户友好的
eg: The new banking app is so user-friendly that even my grandparents can use it.
egCn: 新的银行应用非常好用，连我祖父母都会用。

eg: Hackers broke into the company's system and stole the details of millions of customers.
egCn: 黑客侵入了该公司的系统，窃取了数百万名客户的资料。

eg: Virtual reality allows trainee surgeons to practise operations without risking patients' lives.
egCn: 虚拟现实让实习外科医生无需拿病人生命冒险就能练习手术。

eg: Driverless cars could reduce accidents caused by tired or careless drivers.
egCn: 无人驾驶汽车可以减少因司机疲劳或粗心造成的事故。

eg: Some companies are testing drones that can deliver parcels straight to customers' doors.
egCn: 一些公司正在测试能把包裹直接送到顾客家门口的无人机。

eg: Many people feel pressure to upgrade their phones every year, even when the old one works fine.
egCn: 许多人觉得有压力每年都要换新手机，即使旧的还能正常用。

eg: Many schools still rely on outdated computers that cannot run modern programs.
egCn: 许多学校仍在使用无法运行现代程序的老旧电脑。

eg: The city has attracted several high-tech firms by offering low taxes and good transport links.
egCn: 该市通过提供低税率和便利的交通吸引了几家高科技公司。

eg: Parents are advised to limit their children's screen time to two hours a day.
egCn: 建议家长将孩子每天看屏幕的时间限制在两小时以内。

eg: Streaming services have changed the way people watch films and listen to music.
egCn: 流媒体服务改变了人们看电影和听音乐的方式。

eg: Rapid technological change means that workers must keep learning new skills throughout their careers.
egCn: 技术日新月异，意味着劳动者必须在整个职业生涯中不断学习新技能。

eg: People in remote villages often struggle to get fast broadband for work or study.
egCn: 偏远村庄的人们往往很难用上能满足工作或学习需要的高速宽带。

eg: Most people simply type a question into a search engine instead of opening a book.
egCn: 大多数人遇到问题就直接在搜索引擎里输入，而不是翻书。

eg: Always back up important files in case your laptop is lost or stolen.
egCn: 一定要备份重要文件，以防笔记本电脑丢失或被盗。

eg: Many banks now use chatbots to answer simple customer questions at any time of day.
egCn: 许多银行现在用聊天机器人全天候回答客户的简单问题。

eg: The hospital has invested in cutting-edge equipment to treat cancer more effectively.
egCn: 这家医院投资购置了尖端设备，以更有效地治疗癌症。

eg: Social media algorithms decide which posts we see, often showing us only what we already like.
egCn: 社交媒体的算法决定我们能看到哪些帖子，往往只推送我们本来就喜欢的内容。

eg: Banks spend huge sums on cybersecurity to protect customers from online fraud.
egCn: 银行在网络安全上投入巨资，保护客户免受网络诈骗。

eg: The digital divide means that poorer students often lack the devices they need for online learning.
egCn: 数字鸿沟意味着较贫困的学生往往缺少在线学习所需的设备。

cn: 精通科技的；熟悉电子产品的
eg: Older employees are often less tech-savvy than their younger colleagues, but they learn quickly.
egCn: 年长员工往往不如年轻同事熟悉科技产品，但他们学得很快。

eg: Cloud computing allows small businesses to store files online without buying expensive servers.
egCn: 云计算让小企业无需购买昂贵的服务器就能在线存储文件。

eg: Wearable devices like smartwatches can track your heart rate and sleep patterns.
egCn: 智能手表等可穿戴设备可以监测你的心率和睡眠模式。

eg: Some airports use facial recognition to check passengers' identities in seconds.
egCn: 一些机场使用人脸识别技术，几秒钟就能核验旅客身份。

eg: Constant notifications can lead to information overload and make it harder to concentrate.
egCn: 不断弹出的通知可能导致信息过载，让人更难集中注意力。

eg: Smartphones have made many older gadgets, such as cameras and MP3 players, almost obsolete.
egCn: 智能手机已让相机、MP3 播放器等许多老式电子产品几乎被淘汰。

eg: A balanced diet with plenty of fruit and vegetables lowers the risk of many diseases.
egCn: 富含水果蔬菜的均衡饮食能降低患多种疾病的风险。

eg: Heart disease is still one of the leading causes of death in developed countries.
egCn: 心脏病仍是发达国家的主要死因之一。

eg: Long working hours and poor sleep can increase the risk of serious illness.
egCn: 长时间工作和睡眠不足会增加患重病的风险。

eg: Early treatment greatly improves the chances of a full recovery.
egCn: 及早治疗能大大提高完全康复的几率。

eg: Although the disease cannot be cured, modern drugs help patients live normal lives.
egCn: 这种病虽然无法根治，但现代药物能帮助患者正常生活。

eg: Hospitals are so busy that some patients wait hours before seeing a doctor.
egCn: 医院太忙，一些病人要等好几个小时才能看上医生。

eg: Joining a gym is a popular way for office workers to improve their fitness.
egCn: 办健身卡是上班族提升体能的常见方式。

eg: The number of overweight children has risen sharply over the past twenty years.
egCn: 过去二十年里，超重儿童的数量急剧上升。

eg: Advertising junk food during children's TV programmes should be banned.
egCn: 应该禁止在儿童电视节目中播放垃圾食品广告。

eg: Many people know their habits are unhealthy but find it hard to change them.
egCn: 许多人知道自己的习惯不健康，却很难改掉。

eg: Spending time outdoors has clear benefits for both physical and mental health.
egCn: 多到户外活动对身心健康都有明显的好处。

eg: Office workers often lead a lifestyle that involves sitting down for most of the day.
egCn: 上班族的生活方式往往是一天中大部分时间都坐着。

eg: Common symptoms of the flu include a high temperature, a sore throat and tiredness.
egCn: 流感的常见症状包括高烧、喉咙痛和乏力。

eg: Washing your hands regularly is a simple way to avoid catching an infection.
egCn: 经常洗手是避免感染的简单方法。

eg: After the surgery, she needed several weeks of rest before returning to work.
egCn: 手术后，她需要休息几周才能回去上班。

eg: Exam pressure causes high levels of anxiety among teenagers in many countries.
egCn: 在许多国家，考试压力让青少年普遍处于高度焦虑之中。

eg: Getting enough sleep helps keep your immune system strong during the winter months.
egCn: 睡眠充足有助于在冬季保持免疫系统强健。

eg: This medicine may cause side effects such as headaches and feeling sick.
egCn: 这种药可能会引起头痛、恶心等副作用。

eg: In some countries, antibiotics can be bought without a prescription, which leads to overuse.
egCn: 在一些国家，抗生素无需处方就能买到，导致滥用。

eg: Free healthcare should be available to everyone, regardless of their income.
egCn: 无论收入高低，每个人都应能享受免费医疗。

eg: Gaming addiction has become a growing concern among parents of teenage boys.
egCn: 游戏成瘾已成为青少年男孩家长日益担心的问题。

eg: A broken bone usually takes around six weeks to heal completely.
egCn: 骨折通常需要六周左右才能完全愈合。

eg: Processed food is often cheap and convenient, but it tends to contain a lot of salt.
egCn: 加工食品往往便宜又方便，但通常含盐量很高。

eg: A short workout before breakfast gives me more energy for the rest of the day.
egCn: 早餐前简单锻炼一下，能让我一整天都更有精神。

eg: Talking therapy can be just as effective as medication for some kinds of depression.
egCn: 对某些类型的抑郁症来说，谈话疗法和药物治疗同样有效。

eg: Adults over fifty should have a medical check-up at least once a year.
egCn: 五十岁以上的成年人至少应每年体检一次。

eg: The new vaccine was developed in record time and has saved millions of lives.
egCn: 这款新疫苗以创纪录的速度研发出来，挽救了数百万人的生命。

eg: Childhood obesity is closely linked to sugary drinks and a lack of exercise.
egCn: 儿童肥胖与含糖饮料和缺乏运动密切相关。

eg: Without quick treatment, a serious allergic reaction can be fatal.
egCn: 严重的过敏反应若不及时治疗，可能会致命。

eg: Taking painkillers every day may hide a health problem that needs proper attention.
egCn: 每天吃止痛药可能会掩盖需要认真对待的健康问题。

eg: Schools should provide nutritious lunches so that every child can concentrate in class.
egCn: 学校应提供营养丰富的午餐，让每个孩子都能在课堂上集中精力。

eg: Thanks to better healthcare, average life expectancy has risen by over ten years since 1960.
egCn: 由于医疗条件改善，人均预期寿命自 1960 年以来提高了十多年。

eg: People with chronic conditions such as diabetes need regular medical support.
egCn: 糖尿病等慢性病患者需要定期的医疗支持。

eg: Some experts describe obesity as a modern epidemic affecting rich and poor nations alike.
egCn: 一些专家把肥胖称为一种现代流行病，富国穷国都深受其害。

eg: Measles is highly contagious, so infected children should stay at home.
egCn: 麻疹传染性极强，因此受感染的儿童应待在家中。

eg: The overuse of antibiotics has made some bacteria much harder to kill.
egCn: 滥用抗生素使一些细菌变得更难杀灭。

eg: My uncle was diagnosed with diabetes after a routine blood test.
egCn: 我叔叔在一次常规验血后被诊断出患有糖尿病。

eg: Regular contact with friends is important for our emotional well-being.
egCn: 经常与朋友联系对我们的情绪健康很重要。

eg: Poor hygiene in hospitals can allow infections to spread quickly between patients.
egCn: 医院卫生状况差会让感染在病人之间迅速传播。

cn: 久坐不动的；缺乏运动的
eg: A sedentary job increases the risk of back pain and weight gain.
egCn: 久坐不动的工作会增加腰背痛和体重上升的风险。

eg: I was stuck in a traffic jam for an hour on my way to the airport.
egCn: 我去机场的路上堵了一个小时。
collocations: be stuck in a traffic jam

eg: Cheaper public transport would persuade more people to leave their cars at home.
egCn: 更便宜的公共交通会说服更多人把车留在家里。

eg: The trains are so crowded in the morning that it is hard to find a place to stand.
egCn: 早上的火车太挤了，连站的地方都很难找到。

eg: The shortage of cheap housing forces many young people to live with their parents.
egCn: 廉价住房短缺迫使许多年轻人与父母同住。

eg: In big cities, many workers spend half their salary on rent.
egCn: 在大城市，许多上班族要把一半工资花在房租上。

eg: I grew up in a quiet neighbourhood where everyone knew each other.
egCn: 我在一个安静的街区长大，那里人人都相互认识。

eg: Modern skyscrapers have completely changed the skyline of cities like Shanghai and Dubai.
egCn: 现代摩天大楼彻底改变了上海、迪拜等城市的天际线。

eg: Travelling during rush hour can easily double the time of your journey.
egCn: 在高峰时段出行很容易让路上的时间翻倍。

eg: More families are moving to the countryside in search of cleaner air and lower prices.
egCn: 越来越多的家庭搬到乡村，寻找更清新的空气和更低的物价。

eg: Rising rents have left many low-income families homeless in recent years.
egCn: 近年来房租上涨，使许多低收入家庭无家可归。

eg: The population of the capital has doubled since the 1990s, putting pressure on local services.
egCn: 自二十世纪九十年代以来，首都人口翻了一番，给当地公共服务带来压力。

eg: The council built new cycle lanes to make cycling safer for commuters.
egCn: 市政府新建了自行车道，让通勤骑行更安全。

eg: Urban areas usually offer better job opportunities than small towns.
egCn: 城市地区通常比小城镇提供更好的就业机会。

eg: Young people often leave rural areas because there are few jobs or entertainment options.
egCn: 年轻人常常离开农村，因为那里工作机会少，也缺乏娱乐。

eg: Thousands of people commute into the city every day from towns over fifty miles away.
egCn: 每天有成千上万的人从五十多英里外的城镇通勤进城。

eg: The main shopping street is now closed to cars and open only to pedestrians.
egCn: 主要商业街现在禁止车辆通行，只对行人开放。

eg: Families with young children often move to the suburbs for bigger houses and gardens.
egCn: 有小孩的家庭常常搬到郊区，以便住更大的房子、拥有花园。

eg: Overcrowded flats can damage children's health and make it difficult for them to study.
egCn: 过于拥挤的公寓可能损害孩子的健康，并让他们难以学习。

cn: 负担得起的；价格合理的
eg: The government has promised to build fifty thousand affordable homes in the capital.
egCn: 政府承诺在首都建造五万套经济适用房。

eg: Access to green space helps city residents relax and stay physically active.
egCn: 能接触到绿地有助于城市居民放松身心、保持运动。

eg: Many families in Hong Kong live in high-rise flats with very little living space.
egCn: 香港许多家庭住在居住空间狭小的高层公寓里。

cn: 内城区（常指市中心较贫困的地区）
eg: Schools in the inner city often have fewer resources than those in wealthier suburbs.
egCn: 内城区的学校往往比富裕郊区的学校资源更少。

eg: Heavy lorries should be banned from quiet residential streets at night.
egCn: 夜间应禁止重型卡车驶入安静的居民区街道。

eg: The high cost of living in London pushes many young workers to share flats.
egCn: 伦敦高昂的生活成本迫使许多年轻上班族合租。

eg: Our landlord raised the rent by twenty per cent without making any repairs.
egCn: 我们的房东把房租涨了百分之二十，却什么都没修。

eg: Residents living near the airport complain about noise pollution from planes at night.
egCn: 住在机场附近的居民抱怨夜间飞机带来的噪声污染。

eg: The old clock tower is the best-known landmark in my hometown.
egCn: 那座老钟楼是我家乡最有名的地标。

eg: The council plans to turn the run-down factory district into parks and shops.
egCn: 市政府计划把破败的工厂区改造成公园和商店。

eg: The financial district is busy during the day but almost empty at weekends.
egCn: 金融区白天很繁忙，到周末却几乎空无一人。

eg: Air quality in the city improves noticeably on days when car use is restricted.
egCn: 在限制汽车使用的日子里，城市的空气质量明显改善。

eg: Charging drivers to enter the city centre has reduced congestion in several European capitals.
egCn: 向驶入市中心的司机收费，已经缓解了几个欧洲首都的交通拥堵。

eg: Rapid urbanisation has created huge demand for housing, schools and hospitals.
egCn: 快速城市化带来了对住房、学校和医院的巨大需求。

eg: Millions of people who move to cities end up living in slums without clean water.
egCn: 数百万迁入城市的人最终住进了没有干净饮用水的贫民窟。

eg: Several historic buildings were demolished to make way for a new shopping centre.
egCn: 几座历史建筑被拆除，为新建购物中心腾出地方。
collocations: be demolished to make way for

eg: Large supermarkets are usually built on the outskirts of town where land is cheaper.
egCn: 大型超市通常建在土地更便宜的城郊。

cn: 便利设施；生活设施（常用复数）
eg: New housing estates should include basic amenities such as shops, schools and clinics.
egCn: 新建住宅区应配备商店、学校和诊所等基本生活设施。

eg: Good urban planning puts homes, workplaces and shops within walking distance of each other.
egCn: 良好的城市规划会让住宅、工作场所和商店彼此相距步行可达。

eg: Diseases spread more easily in densely populated areas with poor sanitation.
egCn: 在卫生条件差、人口稠密的地区，疾病更容易传播。

eg: Urban sprawl swallows up farmland and makes people more dependent on cars.
egCn: 城市无序扩张吞噬农田，并使人们更依赖汽车。

cn: 士绅化；中产阶级化（旧城区改造后房价上涨）
eg: Gentrification has improved the area, but long-term residents can no longer afford to live there.
egCn: 士绅化改善了这片地区，但长期居住于此的居民却再也住不起了。

eg: The film was a worldwide success and was translated into more than thirty languages.
egCn: 这部电影风靡全球，被翻译成三十多种语言。

eg: Tourism brings money to poor regions but can also damage local traditions.
egCn: 旅游业给贫困地区带来收入，但也可能破坏当地传统。

eg: Trade between Asia and Europe has grown rapidly over the past three decades.
egCn: 过去三十年里，亚欧之间的贸易迅速增长。

eg: Britain imports much of its fruit from countries with warmer climates.
egCn: 英国的大部分水果是从气候较温暖的国家进口的。

eg: Many developing countries depend on selling raw materials such as coffee and cotton.
egCn: 许多发展中国家依靠出售咖啡、棉花等原材料为生。

eg: People in developed countries tend to use far more energy per person.
egCn: 发达国家的人均能源消耗往往高得多。

eg: The same fashion brands can now be found in shopping malls all over the world.
egCn: 如今世界各地的商场里都能找到同样的时装品牌。

eg: International coffee chains have replaced many traditional tea houses in the city centre.
egCn: 国际连锁咖啡店取代了市中心的许多传统茶馆。

eg: Cheap goods made abroad have put many local manufacturers out of business.
egCn: 国外生产的廉价商品让许多本地制造商倒闭。

eg: Western fast food has become extremely popular among young people in Asia.
egCn: 西式快餐在亚洲年轻人中极受欢迎。

eg: Goods and people now cross national borders more freely than ever before.
egCn: 如今商品和人员跨越国界比以往任何时候都更加自由。

eg: The internet has made the exchange of ideas between countries faster than ever.
egCn: 互联网让各国之间的思想交流比以往任何时候都更快。

eg: Multinational companies often move their factories to countries where wages are lower.
egCn: 跨国公司常常把工厂搬到工资较低的国家。

eg: Foreign trade has lifted millions of people out of poverty in East Asia.
egCn: 对外贸易使东亚数百万人摆脱了贫困。

eg: Supporters of free trade argue that it lowers prices for ordinary consumers.
egCn: 自由贸易的支持者认为，它能降低普通消费者购买商品的价格。

eg: Her grandparents emigrated to Canada in the 1970s to look for better work.
egCn: 她的祖父母于二十世纪七十年代移民加拿大，寻找更好的工作。

eg: Globalisation has raised the standard of living for many, but not for everyone.
egCn: 全球化提高了许多人的生活水平，但并非人人受益。

eg: A weak exchange rate makes a country's exports cheaper for foreign buyers.
egCn: 汇率走弱会让一国的出口商品对外国买家来说更便宜。
collocations: the exchange rate against the dollar

eg: Opening up to foreign trade helped China achieve decades of rapid economic growth.
egCn: 对外开放贸易帮助中国实现了数十年的经济高速增长。

eg: Business travellers often suffer from jet lag after long flights across several time zones.
egCn: 商务旅客在跨越多个时区的长途飞行后常常要倒时差。

eg: The war forced hundreds of thousands of refugees to seek safety in neighbouring countries.
egCn: 战争迫使数十万难民到邻国寻求庇护。

eg: Mass tourism has turned some quiet fishing villages into crowded holiday resorts.
egCn: 大众旅游让一些宁静的渔村变成了拥挤的度假胜地。

eg: Translation apps are helping travellers overcome the language barrier in foreign countries.
egCn: 翻译软件正帮助游客在国外克服语言障碍。

eg: Low taxes and cheap land have attracted foreign investment into the region.
egCn: 低税率和廉价土地吸引了外资进入该地区。

eg: Much of the world's manufacturing has moved to countries with lower labour costs.
egCn: 全球大部分制造业已转移到劳动力成本较低的国家。

eg: Some companies are criticised for relying on cheap labour in poorer countries.
egCn: 一些公司因依赖贫穷国家的廉价劳动力而受到批评。

eg: Critics say globalisation has concentrated wealth in the hands of a small elite.
egCn: 批评者认为，全球化使财富集中到少数精英手中。

eg: Budget airlines have made foreign holidays affordable for millions of ordinary families.
egCn: 廉价航空让数以百万计的普通家庭也能负担得起出国度假。

eg: Working with colleagues in different time zones means some meetings happen late at night.
egCn: 与不同时区的同事共事，意味着有些会议要在深夜召开。

eg: Supermarkets now sell exotic fruits that my grandparents had never even heard of.
egCn: 超市里如今有卖我祖父母闻所未闻的异国水果。

eg: Many Western firms outsource their customer service to call centres in India.
egCn: 许多西方企业把客户服务外包给印度的呼叫中心。

eg: The brain drain means poorer countries lose doctors and engineers they paid to train.
egCn: 人才外流意味着贫穷国家失去了自己花钱培养的医生和工程师。

cn: 相互关联的；相互连接的
eg: In an interconnected world, a financial crisis in one country can quickly spread to others.
egCn: 在相互关联的世界里，一国的金融危机会迅速蔓延到其他国家。

eg: The pandemic showed how fragile global supply chains had become.
egCn: 疫情暴露出全球供应链已变得多么脆弱。

eg: Inequality between rich and poor nations remains one of the biggest challenges of our time.
egCn: 富国与穷国之间的不平等仍是我们这个时代最大的挑战之一。

eg: Raising tariffs on imported steel protects local jobs but makes cars more expensive.
egCn: 提高进口钢材关税能保护本地就业，却会让汽车更贵。

eg: International trade has brought prosperity to port cities for hundreds of years.
egCn: 几百年来，国际贸易一直为港口城市带来繁荣。

eg: London is a truly cosmopolitan city where you can hear dozens of languages on one street.
egCn: 伦敦是一座真正国际化的城市，一条街上就能听到几十种语言。

eg: Thousands of expatriates work in Dubai, attracted by high salaries and tax-free income.
egCn: 数以千计的外籍人士在迪拜工作，被高薪和免税收入吸引。

eg: Economists warn that rising protectionism could slow growth and raise prices worldwide.
egCn: 经济学家警告，日益抬头的贸易保护主义可能拖慢全球经济增长、推高物价。

eg: In the experiment, plants grown under blue light grew faster than the others.
egCn: 在这项实验中，蓝光下培育的植物比其他植物长得更快。

eg: The new vaccine was tested in the laboratory for months before trials on humans began.
egCn: 这种新疫苗在实验室里测试了几个月，之后才开始人体试验。

eg: Scientific progress over the last century has helped people in most countries live much longer.
egCn: 过去一个世纪的科学进步让大多数国家的人寿命大大延长。

eg: The discovery of penicillin in 1928 changed medicine forever.
egCn: 1928 年青霉素的发现彻底改变了医学。

eg: Astronomers have found thousands of planets orbiting stars outside our solar system.
egCn: 天文学家已发现数千颗环绕太阳系外恒星运行的行星。

eg: Astronauts on the space station grow vegetables to study how plants behave without gravity.
egCn: 空间站上的宇航员种植蔬菜，以研究植物在失重环境下的生长情况。

eg: Private companies are now building reusable rockets to cut the cost of space travel.
egCn: 如今私营公司正在制造可重复使用的火箭，以降低太空旅行的成本。

eg: Powerful telescopes allow scientists to see galaxies that formed billions of years ago.
egCn: 强大的望远镜让科学家能看到数十亿年前形成的星系。

eg: Trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the air.
egCn: 树木吸收二氧化碳，向空气中释放氧气。

eg: Jupiter is by far the largest planet in our solar system.
egCn: 木星是太阳系中最大的行星，远超其他行星。

eg: Before electricity was widely available, most people went to bed when it got dark.
egCn: 在电力普及之前，大多数人天一黑就睡觉。

eg: Building a bridge across such a wide river was a remarkable achievement of engineering.
egCn: 在如此宽的河上架起一座桥是一项了不起的工程成就。

eg: Researchers have identified a gene that increases the risk of certain types of cancer.
egCn: 研究人员发现了一种会增加某些癌症患病风险的基因。

eg: Scientists extracted DNA from ancient bones to learn where early humans travelled.
egCn: 科学家从古代骨骼中提取 DNA，以了解早期人类的迁徙路线。

eg: Everything around us, from water to our own bodies, is made of atoms.
egCn: 我们周围的一切，从水到我们自己的身体，都是由原子构成的。

eg: Because gravity on the Moon is much weaker, astronauts can jump very high there.
egCn: 由于月球上的重力弱得多，宇航员在那里能跳得很高。

eg: Weather satellites help forecasters warn people about approaching storms.
egCn: 气象卫星帮助预报员提醒人们风暴即将来临。

eg: Some people argue that space exploration is a waste of money while poverty still exists.
egCn: 有人认为，在贫困依然存在的情况下，太空探索是在浪费钱。

eg: The agency plans to launch a new weather satellite next spring.
egCn: 该机构计划明年春天发射一颗新的气象卫星。

eg: Bacteria are so small that they can only be seen under a microscope.
egCn: 细菌非常小，只有在显微镜下才能看到。

eg: The fossils of sea creatures found in the mountains show that the area was once under water.
egCn: 在山中发现的海洋生物化石表明，这里曾经是一片汪洋。

eg: Many cosmetics companies have stopped animal testing in response to public pressure.
egCn: 迫于公众压力，许多化妆品公司已停止动物实验。

eg: Not all bacteria are harmful; some actually help us to digest food.
egCn: 并非所有细菌都有害，有些其实能帮助我们消化食物。

eg: Nothing, not even light, can escape from the pull of a black hole.
egCn: 任何东西，甚至光，都无法摆脱黑洞的引力。

eg: The spacecraft took seven months to travel from Earth to Mars.
egCn: 这艘航天器花了七个月才从地球飞抵火星。

eg: Careful observation of the night sky led early astronomers to important conclusions.
egCn: 对夜空的细致观测让早期天文学家得出了重要结论。

eg: Water is the only common substance found naturally as a solid, a liquid and a gas.
egCn: 水是唯一在自然界中以固态、液态和气态存在的常见物质。

eg: Scientific progress is often driven by simple curiosity about how the world works.
egCn: 科学进步常常源于人们对世界运作方式的单纯好奇。

eg: So far there is no proof that life exists on any other planet.
egCn: 到目前为止，还没有证据证明其他星球上存在生命。

eg: The physicist spent years trying to explain how light travels through space.
egCn: 这位物理学家花了多年时间，试图解释光是如何在太空中传播的。

eg: A water molecule is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
egCn: 一个水分子由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成。

eg: Some tiny organisms can survive in boiling water or deep under the ice.
egCn: 一些微小的生物能在沸水中或冰层深处生存。

eg: Genetically modified crops can resist pests, but some consumers still worry about their safety.
egCn: 转基因作物能抵抗害虫，但一些消费者仍担心其安全性。

eg: Dolly the sheep, cloned in 1996, was the first mammal copied from an adult cell.
egCn: 1996 年克隆出的多莉羊，是第一只由成年体细胞复制而成的哺乳动物。

eg: The space station completes one orbit of the Earth roughly every ninety minutes.
egCn: 空间站大约每九十分钟绕地球运行一圈。

eg: Our own galaxy, the Milky Way, contains hundreds of billions of stars.
egCn: 我们所在的星系——银河系，包含数千亿颗恒星。

eg: Tiny particles of dust and smoke in the air can damage our lungs.
egCn: 空气中微小的灰尘和烟雾颗粒会损害我们的肺部。

eg: The development of the first vaccine was a major breakthrough in the fight against disease.
egCn: 第一种疫苗的研制是人类对抗疾病的一项重大突破。

eg: Astronauts on long missions are exposed to dangerous levels of radiation from the sun.
egCn: 执行长期任务的宇航员会暴露在来自太阳的危险辐射之下。

eg: Despite decades of searching, scientists have found no clear sign of extraterrestrial life.
egCn: 尽管搜寻了几十年，科学家仍未发现外星生命的明确迹象。
